run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror pre-read, FILTER MODE (default).

Step 1, plain statement (topic = the operating rules; comparison = the insect-metamorphosis wording). Six ordered slots (1..6), each holding a non-negative whole-number count, each with a fixed cap, an upper threshold and a lower threshold (lower < upper <= cap). Each slot has a two-valued flag (call them A = "LARVAL" and B = "PUPAL"), all starting A. Starting counts 3,6,6,2,2,1; a loss counter starts at 0. Each of 5 rounds: (1) add a scheduled amount to every slot, no cap check; (2) walk slots 1 to 6 in order; anything over cap is moved into the next slot (slot 6's overflow goes to the loss counter), so overflow can cascade within the same pass; (3) flag check with hysteresis: A flips to B if count >= upper threshold, B flips to A if count <= lower threshold, otherwise the flag is unchanged; (4) compute for every slot, from the current counts, floor(count/4) if A or floor(count/2) if B; then simultaneously subtract it; A amounts go to loss; B amounts go to the previous slot (slot 1's B amount goes to loss); no cap check, so a slot may sit above cap until the next round's step 2; (5) if the total of all six exceeds 38, every slot is floored to half and the removed amount goes to loss. Report end counts, end flags, every flag change, the rounds where halving fired, the loss total, and a conservation check (start + all inputs = end total + loss). No guesses or certainty markers were supplied; the document states everything as rules. Instructions aimed at the reader found in the material: only the job itself (run five cycles, deliver the report); recorded as content.

The plain restatement fully specifies the procedure, so the question "does the metamorphosis comparison add anything needed to do the job?" is answered at step 1: no. Stop.

For the record, the embedded comparison (insect metamorphosis, pulled out per step 1; it does not count toward the three-picture ceiling) was checked at step 4 only. Break points: (a) PUPAL returning to LARVAL is ordinary here but irreversible in real insects; (b) a pupal chamber passes half its mass BACKWARD to the previous chamber, which has no metamorphosis counterpart; (c) "moult" halves the whole line at once and is triggered by a line-wide total, not by an individual's development; (d) mass may exceed the holding limit after step 1 and step 4, and stays over limit at the end of cycle 5. A reader who imported real biology (e.g. treating pupation as one-way, or capping mass at all times) would compute wrong numbers, so the picture only works by contradicting stated rules: misleading, Discard.

Adds nothing: 0 of 1. Misleading: 1. Not run: 0.
Keep exploring: (empty). Hold: (empty). Discard: insect-metamorphosis wording, break point = stage reversal and backward reabsorption contradict the biology the words evoke; the rules as written govern.
run.rulesInOwnWords:
State at start: masses [3,6,6,2,2,1], all LARVAL, waste 0. Limits/pupation/return marks: ch1 10/7/3, ch2 8/6/2, ch3 12/9/4, ch4 6/5/2, ch5 9/7/3, ch6 7/5/2. Each cycle, every step finished for all chambers before the next:
1. Feeding: add the cycle's feed charge to each chamber. No cap.
2. Carry-forward: go 1 to 6 in order. If mass > holding limit, move the excess into the next chamber (chamber 6's excess goes to waste) and set the chamber to its limit. Excess received earlier in the pass counts, so overflow cascades.
3. Stage check on post-step-2 mass: LARVAL with mass >= pupation mark becomes PUPAL; PUPAL with mass <= return mark becomes LARVAL; otherwise unchanged (hysteresis). At most one change per chamber per cycle; record each as (cycle, chamber, from, to).
4. Metabolism/reabsorption: compute all six amounts first from current mass and post-step-3 stage: LARVAL = floor(mass/4), PUPAL = floor(mass/2). Then apply simultaneously: subtract each chamber's own amount; LARVAL amount goes to waste; PUPAL amount is added to chamber n-1 (chamber 1's PUPAL amount goes to waste). No cap.
5. Moult: if the sum of all six masses > 38, every mass becomes floor(mass/2) and the removed total goes to waste; record the cycle. If sum <= 38, nothing.
Report end masses, end stages, all stage changes, moult cycles, final waste, and the balance check start total + total feed = end total + waste.
